steps: Preheat the oven to 400° F.
Combine all ingredients except the chicken wings in a large bowl.
Add the chicken and toss to coat.
Place the chicken wings in a baking dish and bake for 30 to 35 minutes. Check for doneness.
Serve the wings hot or place in a covered warming dish or crock pot on low setting until ready to serve.
hints: Buy fresh wing drummettes. A 1-1/4 pound package contains approximately 12 drummettes. If unavailable, ask your butcher to cut whole chicken wings into drummette size.
Boneless chicken pieces may be used in this recipe. Check for doneness after 20 minutes.
Choose lowest sodium brand barbecue sauce or instead of using commercial barbecue sauce, serve with DaVita.com’s recipe for Zesty Barbecue Sauce. Sodium content is much lower.
Look for the lowest sodium brand of green chili peppers. Sodium varies greatly between brands.

title: Minted Lemonade
description: Quench your thirst with a refreshing glass of Minted Lemonade. This kidney-friendly recipe features the right balance of lemon, mint and sweetner for a delicious beverage you’ll be sipping all summer long.
steps: In a 1-quart pitcher, mix lemon juice, sugar and mint leaves. Add 3-1/2 cups of cold water to fill the pitcher.
Chill until cold.
Serve in a 6-ounce glass with a sprig of mint to garnish.
hints: For a stronger mint flavor crush the mint leaves.
To reduce carbohydrate and calories substitute Splenda® sweetener for sugar (12 packets or 1/2 cup Splenda® granular. Calories are reduced to 16 and carbohydrate to 4 grams.

title: New England Lobster Rolls
description: The key to a great lobster roll is to keep it simple. Toasted buns filled with lobster mixed with mayonnaise, lemon juice, celery and hot sauce makes these New England Lobster Rolls great!
steps: Steam lobster until meat is opaque, about 5 to 6 minutes. Let cool then cut lobster into bite-sized pieces. Finely chop celery while lobster is cooking.
Combine mayo, celery, lemon juice and hot sauce. Add lobster meat and toss to coat.
Split buns and spread with butter. Toast in a skillet.
Make lobster rolls by dividing the lobster mixture between the 4 buns. Serve with lemon wedges.
hints: Buy regular hotdog buns if split-top hotdog rolls are unavailable.
Look for fresh or frozen lobster meat or lobster tails, or cook a whole lobster. Two 6-ounce lobster tails work great.
Lobster meat is naturally high in sodium. Select lower sodium foods for your remaining meals to stay within your sodium limit.

title: Twice-Baked Apple Cake
description: Enjoy the smell of baked apples, cinnamon and cake with kidney-friendly Twice-Baked Apple Cake.
steps: Preheat oven to 350° F. Grease a 9-inch spring form pan.

Cut 4 tablespoons of the margarine into pieces. With the food processor metal blade in place, add 2/3 cup sugar, flour, 4 tablespoons margarine, baking soda, vanilla and one egg to food processor bowl. Process until mixture resembles cornmeal. Spread mixture in the bottom of well-greased pan.
Peel, quarter and seed apples. Insert slicing disk in food processor and stand apple quarters upright in feed tube. Slice using moderate pressure on the pusher.
Arrange apple slices in layers on top of the crumb mixture. Bake for 45 minutes.

While cake is baking, add remaining 3 tablespoons sugar, remaining 3 tablespoons margarine (melted), cinnamon and one egg to the bowl of the food processor fitted with the metal blade. Process until the mixture is smooth and sugar dissolves. Spoon mixture over apples and bake 30 minutes more or until top is firm.
hints: Recommended apple varieties include Cortland, Pippin, Rome or your personal favorite.
If you do not have a food processor, use a blender to mix the cake and topping.

title: No Fuss Microwave Egg White French Toast
description: While chefs in fancy restaurants may be labeled “creative” when whipping up recipes, a renal dietitian uses that same creativity to help kidney patients enjoy their healthy diets. DaVita dietitian Susan from Oregon shares her delicious No Fuss Microwave Egg White French Toast— a fantastic low sugar, low fat breakfast that can also be chilled and eaten like bread pudding. Double yum!
steps: Spread butter over bread or English muffin. Cut into cubes.
Place buttered bread cubes in a microwave-safe bowl.
Pour egg whites over bread to cover.
Sprinkle syrup on top.
Microwave for 1 minute; push up edges of egg white to let uncooked egg out to edges.
Microwave another minute or until egg is set.
hints: Serve warm as French toast or chill and eat as bread pudding.
Egg whites provide excellent quality protein with minimal phosphorus or fat.
If desired substitute 2 whole eggs, beaten for 1/2-cup egg white. This change will increase nutrients to 288 calories, 15 g fat, 434 mg cholesterol and 226 mg phosphorus; sodium is reduced to 353 mg.
If desired, substitute natural maple syrup or cinnamon sugar for lite or sugar-free syrup.
This recipe works well with an English muffin half instead of a slice of bread.

title: Classic Challah
description: Challah is a simple yeast bread served on the Sabbath and Jewish holidays. Try this classic challah from Maryam.
steps: Place the flour, yeast, sugar, water and oil in a large bowl and mix together. Knead the dough. When a ball is formed add the salt. Place the dough on a floured surface and continue kneading for 10 minutes, until dough is smooth and soft and not sticky.
Coat the bowl and dough with 1 to 2 teaspoons of oil. Cover the bowl and set it in a warm place until the dough doubles in volume (1 to 2 hours).
Knead risen dough for a few minutes. Divide the dough into 12 pieces and roll each piece into a strand to be braided, approximately 10″ to 12″ in length.
Braid 3 of the rolled dough strips together to form the challah. Repeat with remaining dough strips to make 4 challahs.
Place challahs on a baking sheet or in a baking pan, cover and let the dough rise again, approximately 40 minutes.

Preheat oven to 350º F. Brush each challah with beaten egg. Bake for approximately 30 minutes, until the challahs turn golden brown. Remove challahs from the oven and from baking pan and cool on a wire rack.
hints: Divide each challah into 8 portions for a total of 32 portions for the 4 loaves.
Sprinkle poppy or sesame seeds on top before baking if desired.
Check YouTube for online videos with instructions on braiding and shaping the challahs.

title: Soda Pop Bread
description: Soda Pop Bread is not your typical quick bread. It calls for soda pop mixed with savory flavors to create a unique bread that is sure to "pop" your taste buds.
steps: Preheat the oven to 350˚ F.
In a medium bowl combine flour, sugar, baking powder and salt. Mix well.
Add the eggs and garlic and mix. Add the root beer and cayenne. Mix all ingredients together well.
Pour the mixture into a greased 9 x 5-inch bread loaf pan.
Bake for 55 to 65 minutes. Let the loaf cool before removing from the pan.
hints: Use less cayenne pepper if you don’t like the heat.

Instead of using root beer and cayenne, try one of these substitutions: 12 ounces ginger ale and 1/3 cup fresh chopped rosemary leaves; or 12 ounces Orange Crush® or Orange Sunkist® soda with 1 tablespoon ground basil; or 12 ounces lemon lime soda with 1/2 cup chopped fresh cilantro.
Root beer, ginger ale, orange soda and lemon lime soda generally do not have phosphorus additives. However, always check the ingredient list for phosphate additives.

title: Stuffed French Toast
description: Transform leftover French bread into a delicious kidney-friendly morning meal, Stuffed French Toast, that you can make the night before and then just pop into the oven in the morning.
ingredients: 1 pound loaf of day-old French bread
steps: Cut bread loaf into 16 slices.
Spread 1 tablespoon cream cheese on each slice of bread. Top with 1 tablespoon jelly and add bread slice to make a sandwich. Repeat until 8 sandwiches are made.
Spray a 9” x 13” baking dish with nonstick cooking spray and place the 8 sandwiches in the dish.
Beat eggs and then mix with milk and vanilla extract. Pour over the bread slices, turning to coat the slices evenly. Cover and refrigerate overnight.
Preheat oven to 350° F. Cover pan with foil and bake for 1 hour. The last 5 minutes of baking, remove the foil to brown the top.
hints: Bring cream cheese to room temperature so it is easier to spread.
Serving suggestions: drizzle with syrup, garnish with fresh fruit and whipped cream or dust with powdered sugar.

This recipe is a good source of protein and calories, a great choice for a high-energy breakfast. Try this different spin on French Toast. It is a good use for leftover bread. Also, preparing this recipe the night before leaves you with nothing left to do in the morning except bake and serve. It’s perfect for brunch.
Compare breads and select the lower sodium brand.

title: Strawberry Fields Forever
description: Strawberry Fields Forever isn’t just the title of a Beatles song, it’s also a refreshing strawberry dish shared by DaVita renal dietitian Sandee from California. Sandee’s Strawberry Fields Forever kidney-friendly recipe combines the sweet flavors of fresh fruit with savory balsamic vinegar. It’s an effortless recipe that can stand on its own, or be a welcome topping on a salad, cake or frozen treat.
ingredients: 2 tablespoons Splenda® No Calorie Sweetener, granular
steps: Wash strawberries with hulls (otherwise, water will seep into middle part causing strawberries to become soggy).
Take off hulls with paring knife.
Cut strawberries into halves.
Place strawberries in a bowl and drizzle with vinegar, and sprinkle with Splenda®.
Stir gently to combine.
Cover and refrigerate for a few hours, preferably over night.
Just before serving grind pepper over strawberries.
hints: Take strawberries out of refrigerator 10 minutes before serving to take away the chill.
Can be served as a topping on angel food cake.
If desired, use sugar or other tabletop sweeteners instead of Splenda®.

title: Fresh Apple Cake with Cream Cheese Frosting
description: Apples, cinnamon, pecans and cream cheese all put together in a tasty kidney-friendly cake thanks to Bev and renal dietitian Nancy from California. Serve it for everyday dessert or at a special occasion. Your guests will never guess this is a low sodium, low potassium, low phosphorus cake.
steps: Preheat oven to 350º F. Spray 9″ x 13″ baking pan with non-stick cooking spray.
Set cream cheese out to soften. Peel, core and chop apples.
Mix together eggs, oil, sugar and 2 teaspoons vanilla. Stir in apples.
In a separate bowl, stir together flour, cinnamon, baking soda and pecans.
Add dry mixture to apple mixture and mix together.
Put into baking pan and bake for one hour. Allow to cool.
For icing, using a mixer, mix together cream cheese, powdered sugar and remaining vanilla.
Spread icing over cake after it has cooled.
hints: For people with diabetes, leave off the icing to reduce calories to 252 and carbohydrate to 33 g. Count as 2 carbohydrate choices.
To reduce fat you can replace half the oil with unsweetened applesauce.

Pecans are high in potassium and phosphorus. The amount contributed to one piece of cake is minimal as long as the recommended portion is followed. Otherwise you can reduce to 1/2 cup pecans or leave them out.

title: Creamy Pasta Primavera
description: DaVita renal dietitian Mary from California enjoys trying different ethnic dishes and making them kidney-friendly so her dialysis patients can eat them too. If you have a taste for Italian, try Mary’s Creamy Pasta Primavera.
ingredients: 8 ounces whole wheat bow tie pasta, uncooked
3/4 cup Rice Dream® Original Classic rice drink
steps: Slice carrots, chop green onion, and cube cream cheese .
Prepare pasta as directed on package (without salt). During last 5 minutes of cooking time, add broccoli and carrots to water. Drain.
Mix cream cheese, Rice Dream®, Parmesan cheese, onion and seasonings in a large saucepan; cook on low heat until cream cheese is melted and mixture is well blended, stirring frequently.
Add pasta and vegetables together; toss lightly and serve hot.
hints: For a higher protein dish add chicken or shrimp.
Frozen broccoli and carrots can be substituted for the fresh vegetables.
Enriched rice milk contains added phosphorus and calcium. Look for the unenriched products.

title: Flatbread Veggie Wrap with Homemade Hummus
description: This wrap includes beautiful vegetables along with a unique and easy homemade hummus. Sure to become a new favorite recipe.
steps: Slice red onion and quarter the cherry tomatoes. Slice the red bell pepper and carrot into thin strips. Mince the garlic clove.
Heat the flat bread one at time in hot pan over medium heat, 3-4 minutes per side.
Whisk together minced garlic, plain Greek yogurt, ground black pepper, olive oil, tahini, lemon juice, ground cumin, and garlic powder in a bowl.
Spread sauce evenly over each pita bread.
Layer onion, tomato, bell pepper, carrot and spinach on each flat bread, split evenly between the two flat breads.
Sprinkle feta over the vegetables and fold or roll the flatbread around the vegetables.
hints: If Greek flat bread is unavailable, other types of flat bread may be substituted. Look on the food label for the brand with the lowest sodium level and carbohydrate level if you are on a lower carbohydrate diet.
Use left over Greek yogurt as a dip or in place of sour cream. The left-over carrot and bell pepper can be dipped into the Greek yogurt for a snack.

title: Cucumber-Carrot Salad
description: Cucumber-Carrot Salad is a cool, crisp and kidney-friendly recipe from the Salads section of DaVita.com.
ingredients: 1/2 teaspoon Mrs. Dash® Italian Medley seasoning blend
steps: Combine rice vinegar, sugar, olive oil and black pepper in a medium bowl. Stir with a whisk.
Cut the 1/2 cucumber in half vertically, remove seeds and slice. Slice carrots and green onion. Finely chop bell pepper.
Add carrots, onion, red bell pepper, cucumber and Mrs. Dash to vinegar mixture; toss to coat.
Cover and chill 30 minutes.
hints: Select unseasoned rice vinegar or substitute cider vinegar if unavailable. Avoid seasoned rice vinegar, as it contains 240 milligrams of sodium for only one tablespoon.

title: Apple Fritter Rings
description: Who doesn’t like Apple Fritter? Enjoy kidney-friendly Apple Fritter Rings the next time you make breakfast.
ingredients: Oil for deep fat frying, about 3/4 cup
steps: Peel and core apples. Cut each apple into 5 rings, approximately 1/2″ thick each.
In a mixing bowl, sift together flour, 2 tablespoons sugar and baking powder.
In a separate bowl combine egg, milk, almond milk and 1 teaspoon oil.
Add egg mixture to dry ingredients and stir until just blended.
In a skillet that is at least 2″ deep, heat 1″ of cooking oil to 375º F.
Dip apple slices in batter one at a time. Fry in hot oil about 1-1/2 minutes until golden brown. Drain on paper towels.
Combine remaining 1/4 cup sugar with cinnamon and sprinkle on fritters. Serve hot.
hints: Donut shop apple fritters contain approximately 300 mg sodium compared to 33 mg per fritter in this recipe.
Splenda® granular sugar substitute can be used instead of sugar, if desired.

title: Homemade Turkey Sausage
description: Enjoy Homemade Turkey Sausage for your next kidney-friendly breakfast.
steps: Crush the fennel seed.
In a small bowl combine turkey with crushed fennel seed, garlic powder, onion powder and salt. Cover the bowl and refrigerate overnight.
Divide the seasoned turkey into portions about the size of a ping-pong ball and flatten into patties to cook.
Cook over medium heat in a nonstick skillet until browned, about 1 to 2 minutes per side.
hints: Extra patties may be frozen for later use. Be sure to place a double layer of wrap or waxed paper between portions to make it easy to separate patties.

title: Fruited Curry Chicken Salad
description: A DaVita dietitian introduces a delicious, simple, kidney-friendly recipe that satisfy any craving. Fruited Curry Chicken Salad is a fresh dish mixing natural fruit sweetness with savory spices.
steps: Dice chicken. Chop celery, onion and apple. Drain and chop water chestnuts.
In a large salad bowl, combine the chicken, celery, onion, apple, grapes, water chestnuts, pepper, curry powder and mayonnaise.
Toss all together.
Serve immediately or chill for later.
hints: To save time, use half a rotisserie chicken with the skin and bones removed.

title: Teriyaki Wings
description: Put an Asian spin on regular chicken wings with this kidney-friendly recipe, Teriyaki Wings.
steps: Place chicken wings in a large zip-lock bag.
Add all ingredients and shake to mix and coat.Refrigerate overnight to marinate.
Preheat oven to 400° F.
Place wing drummettes in a baking dish and bake for 30 to 35 minutes. Check for doneness.
Serve hot or place in a covered warming dish or crock pot on low setting until ready to serve.
hints: Regular soy sauce and teriyaki sauce are extremely high in sodium. Reduced-sodium soy sauce and teriyaki sauce contain less sodium, but are still considered high in sodium content. Be cautious to use only the amount required in the recipe.
Buy fresh wing drummettes at the grocery. A 1-1/4 pound package contains 12 drummettes. If unavailable, ask your butcher to cut whole chicken wings into drummette size.
Boneless chicken pieces may be used in this recipe. Check for doneness after 20 minutes.

title: Kool-Aid Smoothie
description: Kelly’s Kool-Aid® Smoothie is a great way to add a quick, kidney-friendly treat to your dialysis diet.
ingredients: 2 teaspoons Kool-Aid® liquid drink flavor enhancer (any flavor)
steps: Place all ingredients in a blender.
Blend until smooth and serve immediately.
hints: Kool-Aid® Liquid Drink Mix does not contain phosphate additives like the powdered Kool-Aid.

title: Sautéed Cabbage with Mustard Sauce
description: The kidney-friendly recipe for Sauteed Cabbage with Mustard Sauce is a delicious vegetable dish that will have people coming back for seconds.
steps: Make mustard sauce by combining vinegar, mustard, olive oil, apple cider and caraway seeds.
Chop cabbage into bite-size chunks.
Spray nonstick skillet with cooking spray and heat over medium heat. Add cabbage and sauté 8 to 10 minutes, stirring several times.
Pour mustard sauce over cabbage and stir. Reduce to low heat, cover pan and simmer for 5 minutes to combine flavors.
hints: Serve as a side vegetable dish or use as a topping on a hot beef sandwich.
Do not substitute Chinese (napa) cabbage—potassium content is much higher.

title: Banana Pudding Dessert
description: Banana Pudding Dessert is a delicious way to end the day. If you are on dialysis or follow a low potassium diet, remember that bananas are high in potassium, so this banana-flavored dessert is the perfect way to satisfy your craving for a fresh banana.
ingredients: 2 boxes Jell-O Cook and Serve® banana cream pudding mix (3.5 ounce boxes)
steps: Line bottom of a 9” x 13” pan with vanilla wafers.
In a medium saucepan mix 2 boxes banana pudding mix with 2-1/2 cups rice milk. Bring to a boil over medium heat, stirring constantly.
Pour pudding mixture over vanilla wafers
Put second layer of vanilla wafers over first, pressing each one down gently.
Refrigerate for 1 hour. Spread whipped topping over top of chilled dessert.
Return to refrigerator for at least 2 hours before serving.
hints: Substitute sugar-free pudding mix to reduce carbohydrate content to 32 grams and 2 carbohydrate choices.
If you are not on a potassium restricted diet, top vanilla wafers with a layer of sliced bananas.
Check whipped topping ingredients and choose a brand that does not contain phosphate additives.

title: Blackberry Sauce
description: Looking for a sweet, low-potassium fruit treat to top waffles, pancakes and angel food cake? Try scrumptious and kidney-friendly Blackberry Sauce made with delicious fresh or frozen blackberries. Created by the DaVita renal dietitian team, Blackberry Sauce perks up breakfast or dessert.
steps: Crush berries then combine with 1 cup water and sugar in a large saucepan. Bring mixture to a boil.
Combine cornstarch with 2 tablespoons water. Mix well and stir into blackberry mixture. Cook 1 minute over medium high heat to thicken sauce, stirring constantly.
Remove from heat and add lemon juice. Chill in refrigerator until ready to serve.
hints: Use fresh or frozen blackberries.
Serve Blackberry Sauce over angel food cake, sponge cake, pancakes or waffles.
Sugar substitute may be used to replace sugar. Carbohydrate is reduced to 6 grams per serving; carbohydrate choice is reduced to 1/2.

title: Creamy Chicken and Fresh Pepper Chowder
description: Poblano peppers plus red and green bell peppers combined with chicken, low-sodium broth, cream cheese and seasonings are the ingredients that produce this easy, tasty Creamy Chicken and Fresh Pepper Chowder.
steps: Chop the poblano and bell peppers and onion. Chop the cilantro. Cut cream cheese into cubes and set out to soften.

Place chicken breasts, broth, cumin, garlic powder and black pepper in large saucepan. Bring to a boil and cook for 10 to 12 minutes, until chicken is no longer pink. Remove chicken and cut into bite size pieces; keep warm.
Add bay leaf, peppers, onion and cream cheese to stock and simmer until vegetables are tender.
Add chicken back to saucepan and simmer 10 to 15 minutes.
Ladle into bowls and sprinkle each serving with cilantro and 1 tablespoon cheddar cheese.
hints: Some fresh chicken breast meat is “plumped” or “injected” with a saltwater solution which may also contain phosphorus or potassium. Look for fresh chicken breasts that do not include “15% solution” on the package.

title: Chicken Fruit Salad
description: The combination of protein and fruit make this kidney-friendly recipe, Chicken Fruit Salad, a great meal for lunch or dinner.
steps: Cube cooked chicken. Slice celery and slice grapes into halves. Drain mandarin oranges.
Cook pasta according to package, omitting the salt. Drain and rinse in cold water to cool. Drain well.
In a large bowl, combine cooked pasta and all ingredients. Mix well to combine.
Cover and refrigerate until serving time.
hints: This salad tends to taste better the second day as leftovers.
Use reduced-fat mayonnaise if desired. Look for the lowest sodium brand.

title: Zucchini Casserole
description: Summer squash makes a great side dish. DaVita renal dietitian, Arlene from California, provides a delicious kidney-friendly recipe for Zucchini Casserole.
ingredients: 1/2 teaspoon Mrs. Dash® herb seasoning blend
steps: Preheat oven to 325° F.
Chop onion. Grate or chop zucchini. Cut cream cheese and bread into cubes.
Combine eggs, nondairy creamer, onion, salt, pepper and Mrs. Dash® seasoning. Mix well.
Add zucchini, cream cheese and bread cubes. Stir and let stand for 10 minutes.
Spray a small casserole dish with nonstick cooking spray. Pour mixture into dish and bake 45 minutes until casserole is lightly browned and puffy.
hints: Suggested casserole dish size is 6″ x 7-1/2″ or 7″ round.
For variation, prepare with any summer squash.

title: Microwave High Protein Rice Crispy Treats
description: Sweet, buttery and crunchy–that’s how patients describe these yummy Microwave High Protein Rice Krispy Treats from DaVita dietitian Kristen in New Jersey
steps: In a large bowl, melt butter in microwave for 1 minute.
Add marshmallow crème and microwave for 30 seconds; stir. Microwave 30 seconds more and stir until well blended.
Quickly add protein powder and mix until smooth.
Quickly add pre-measured rice crispy cereal and mix until coated.
Pour into a greased 13” x 9” pan and press down evenly.
Cool, and then cut into 12 bars, 3” x 4” each.
hints: After protein powder is added mix quickly and add rice crispy cereal in as soon as possible because the protein powder will start to harden as it cools.

Nutrition facts based on use with EAS 100% Whey Protein powder. One half cup weighs 84 grams and contains 54 grams protein. Since protein powders vary in the amount of protein, phosphorus and calcium, ask your dietitian for a list of acceptable brands.
These treats are great for a snack, dessert, or breakfast on the go!
Marshmallow crème is also known as marshmallow fluff. You can substitute 40 large marshmallows for 2 cups of marshmallow crème.
Compared to the other High Protein Rice Treats recipe on DaVita.com, this version has less protein powder so it is less dense. Both are very tasty!

title: Roasted Maple Cinnamon Pears
description: Three ingredients and 4 steps in this delicious recipe for Roasted Maple Cinnamon Pears makes it super simple. Plus this recipe can be served as a dessert topped with whipped cream or as a breakfast with Greek yogurt and kidney-friendly homemade granola.
steps: Preheat the oven to 400° F. Line a small baking sheet with parchment paper.
Cut pears in half and scoop out the core.
Place pears on baking sheet, then drizzle with maple syrup and sprinkle with cinnamon.
Bake for 20 minutes. Serve warm.
hints: Use 100% pure maple syrup for best flavor. Honey or non-nutritive sweetener such as stevia, sweet leaf sweet drops or Splenda may be used instead of maple syrup or omit sweetener. Roasting brings out the natural sweetness and the cinnamon adds extra flavor.
Experiment with additional spices such as nutmeg, clove or cardamom.
Serve as a breakfast dish with 1/2 cup vanilla Greek yogurt and 1/2 cup Apple Cinnamon Maple Granola, another recipe from Brittany.
